info.name: Predi-Book API
info.description:
API collection for the predi-book backend — real-time aggregated order book for Polymarket + Kalshi.

Base URL: http://localhost:8000
WebSocket: Socket.IO namespace at /orderbook

request.description: Returns server uptime, timestamp, and WebSocket stream stats (active rooms + subscriber counts per namespace).

Socket.IO namespace at /orderbook. Use Postman's Socket.IO request type (not HTTP GET — this entry is for documentation only).

Connect to: http://localhost:8000/orderbook

Client events:
  emit('subscribe', { conditionId, kalshiTicker })
    → server emits 'subscribed' { success: true, room: '<conditionId>:<kalshiTicker>' }
    → server immediately emits 'data' with current aggregated book snapshot

  emit('unsubscribe', { conditionId, kalshiTicker })
    → server emits 'unsubscribed' { success: true, room }

Server events:
  'data' — AggregatedBook emitted on every order book update:
  {
    bids: [{ price, size, venue }],   // sorted desc
    asks: [{ price, size, venue }],   // sorted asc
    polymarket: { bids, asks },       // raw Polymarket YES book
    kalshi:     { bids, asks },       // raw Kalshi YES book (normalised to 0-1)
    updatedAt: ISO timestamp
  }
  venue is one of: 'polymarket' | 'kalshi' | 'both'
  price is a 0–1 decimal string (e.g. '0.65')

  'subscribed'   — ack for subscribe event
  'unsubscribed' — ack for unsubscribe event
  'error'        — { success: false, message }

Behaviour:
  - First subscriber for a market pair opens one Polymarket WS + one Kalshi WS (singleton)
  - Subsequent subscribers for the same pair reuse existing connections
  - When the last subscriber leaves, both WS connections are torn down
  - On reconnect, connections re-open automatically

variable.description: Same host — Socket.IO uses HTTP upgrade
Polymarket market condition ID (from CLOB REST: GET https://clob.polymarket.com/markets/<slug>)
